cards.claim: Polyak momentum preserves the best small-batch data-scaling exponent over a substantially wider batch-size range than SGD, enlarging the critical batch size
cards.conditions: Power-law kernel regression with capacity exponent d > 2, label-noise-dominated setting (constant-order noise), fixed data budget, optimal learning rate and momentum tuned per batch-size regime
cards.effect: Polyak enables larger batch sizes without sacrificing data efficiency; critical batch exponent β*_Polyak > β*_SGD
cards.evidence: Theorem 6.3 and batch-size phase diagram analysis showing critical batch exponents
cards.quote: Polyak preserves the best small-batch scaling over a substantially wider batch-size range

cards.claim: Nesterov momentum achieves better data efficiency than Polyak and SGD in the large-batch regime, improving the achievable data-scaling exponent
cards.conditions: Large batch sizes (β in [β*_SGD, β*_Polyak]), power-law kernel regression, label-noise-dominated, optimal hyperparameters tuned per regime
cards.effect: In large-batch regime, Nesterov data-scaling exponent ≥ Polyak exponent ≥ SGD exponent, with Nesterov attaining best rate at intermediate batch exponent
cards.evidence: Theorem 6.3, Figure 1 showing three-regime batch-size phase diagram and comparative scaling exponents
cards.quote: Nesterov further improves the achievable data-scaling rate within the large batch regime

cards.claim: Critical learning rate for Polyak momentum scales as α_c^Polyak ~ B^{-1/2} + β, allowing higher per-sample effective learning rates than SGD as batch size grows
cards.conditions: Large batch size B, high momentum β approaching 1, power-law kernel regression, sufficient momentum in admissible region
cards.effect: Polyak maintains higher per-sample effective learning rate (order one) as B increases, whereas SGD's admissible per-sample ELR shrinks as B^{-1/2}
cards.evidence: Theorem 4.3 on critical learning-rate scaling for Polyak and discussion of per-sample effective learning rate
cards.quote: Thus, as the batch size grows, the admissible per-sample ELR of SGD shrinks as B^{-1/2}, while Polyak can keep it at order one by increasing proportionally with √B

cards.claim: Nesterov momentum permits substantially higher momentum in large-batch training than Polyak due to stronger batch-size compensation in its stability condition
cards.conditions: Large batch size B, power-law kernel regression, risk stability analysis, high-momentum regime (β near 1)
cards.effect: Nesterov's critical learning rate scales as α_c^Nesterov ~ √(1-β)/√B, compared to Polyak's α_c^Polyak ~ B^{-1/2} + β; √(1-β) << 1-β for β near 1
cards.evidence: Theorem 4.3 critical learning-rate scalings and discussion of batch-size compensation differences between methods
cards.quote: Since √(1-β) << 1-β for β near 1, Nesterov permits substantially higher momentum in large-batch training

cards.claim: Stronger momentum requires correspondingly larger batch size to maintain risk stability; this batch-size compensation is stronger (√B vs √B) for Nesterov than Polyak in high-momentum regime
cards.conditions: Risk stability framework, power-law kernel regression, high-momentum regime, sufficient batch size
cards.effect: Momentum and batch size are jointly coupled for stability; Nesterov's look-ahead provides stronger coupling, allowing higher momentum at fixed batch or requiring less batch-size increase for same momentum gain
cards.evidence: Theorem 4.3 on critical learning-rate scaling showing different β dependencies: Polyak α_c ~ B^{-1/2} + β vs Nesterov α_c ~ √(1-β)/√B
cards.quote: stronger momentum requires a correspondingly larger batch to maintain stability. This compensation scales as √B for Polyak but as √B for Nesterov

cards.claim: Nesterov's look-ahead mechanism suppresses noise accumulation compared to Polyak, reducing the asymptotic noise floor in high-momentum regimes
cards.conditions: Mixed-damping or high-momentum regime, power-law kernel regression with constant-order label noise, large batch size
cards.effect: Nesterov achieves lower noise floor than Polyak; noise floor reduction factor depends on batch size and momentum, improving data efficiency in large-batch regime
cards.evidence: Theorem 5.2 on Nesterov scaling laws showing noise floor scales as B^{-α/2}/√B vs Polyak's noise floor, and discussion of curvature-adaptive damping
cards.quote: Nesterov achieves better data efficiency in the large batch regime because its look-ahead mechanism suppresses noise accumulation

cards.claim: Polyak momentum's risk dynamics in mixed-damping regime behave like SGD with effective learning rate α_eff = α(1+β)/(1-β), preserving the signal-noise tradeoff across batch sizes
cards.conditions: Polyak momentum, power-law kernel regression, mixed-damping regime, high momentum β approaching 1
cards.effect: Signal and noise terms scale identically to SGD but at enlarged effective learning rate proportional to (1+β)/(1-β); allows operating at larger admissible per-sample learning rate while maintaining SGD's risk tradeoff
cards.evidence: Theorem 5.1 analysis of Polyak scaling laws and effective learning rate discussion in Section 4
cards.quote: The overdamped modes evolve with the rescaled learning rate α(1+β)/(1-β), which plays the role of the effective learning rate for momentum. [...] leaving the signal–noise tradeoff unchanged

cards.claim: Nesterov's look-ahead induces curvature-adaptive damping that more strongly damps sharp (high-curvature) directions while preserving dynamics in flat directions
cards.conditions: Nesterov momentum, power-law kernel regression, underdamped spectral regime, varying curvatures across spectral directions
cards.effect: Reduces underdamped transient decay time in sharp directions; suppresses noise accumulation without changing asymptotic signal learning; enables better convergence in mixed-damping regime
cards.evidence: Section 3.3 analysis of Nesterov look-ahead on quadratic functions and Theorem 5.2 showing suppressed underdamped transient
cards.quote: This suppresses the underdamped transient from [...] leaving the asymptotic power-law signal term unchanged at [...]. The same mechanism also suppresses stochastic noise accumulation

cards.claim: At small batch sizes, SGD, Polyak, and Nesterov achieve identical optimal data-scaling exponent; at large batch sizes they separate with Nesterov > Polyak > SGD; at ultra-large batches Nesterov and Polyak equalize and both exceed SGD
cards.conditions: Power-law kernel regression, fixed data budget, batch-size exponent β varying across regimes defined by critical exponents β*_SGD < β*_Polyak < β*_Nesterov, hyperparameters optimized per regime
cards.effect: Three-regime phase diagram in batch-size vs data-scaling exponent space; Polyak extends small-batch regime to larger batches; Nesterov dominates in intermediate large-batch window; step-count limits dominate at ultra-large batch
cards.evidence: Theorem 6.3 batch-size-dependent data scaling with three transition exponents; Figure 1 visualizing phase diagram
cards.quote: Theorem 6.3 shows that the achievable data efficiency depends sharply on batch-size scaling. [...] For β ∈ [β*_SGD, β*_Polyak], Nesterov outperforms Polyak, which in turn outperforms SGD, with Nesterov attaining its best data-scaling rate at β = β*_Nesterov

cards.claim: Momentum's batch-size compensation mechanism differs fundamentally between Polyak and Nesterov: Polyak enlarges critical batch size via multiplicative momentum effect on per-sample ELR, while Nesterov does so via curvature-adaptive noise suppression
cards.conditions: Power-law kernel regression, high-momentum regime, large batch size, label-noise-dominated setting
cards.effect: Polyak maintains SGD signal-noise tradeoff at enlarged effective learning rate; Nesterov improves the tradeoff itself through noise reduction, resulting in different batch-size dependences of optimal data-scaling exponent
cards.evidence: Comparison of Theorems 5.1 and 5.2 (Polyak vs Nesterov scaling laws) and discussion in introduction and Section 4 on why momentum helps
cards.quote: Polyak preserves the SGD signal–noise tradeoff while operating at the enlarged effective learning rate [...], whereas Nesterov further suppresses noise accumulation at large [batch size] through the curvature-adaptive damping induced by its look-ahead mechanism
